findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "verify_phone" references sensitive artifacts (session token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Finish signup: check the 6-digit code the user received by email (or text), activate the workspace and return a session token.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "order_catalog" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_phone, p1_practice_deck, support_status · Private data: verify_phone, dbpr_preview, support_report, tendeck_help, connectors_catalog · Public sink: start_workspace, verify_phone.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_phone, p1_practice_deck, support_status · Private data: verify_phone, dbpr_preview, support_report, tendeck_help, connectors_catalog · Public sink: start_workspace, verify_phone

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
